title: JavaScript and TypeScript: language, browser and Node applications
summary: 42 lessons in JavaScript and TypeScript, from first expressions to asynchronous programs, browser behavior, types and testing. Use worked examples, independent practice and separate reference solutions.

lessons.title: JavaScript, Node and the browser
lessons.outcome: JavaScript is a language; Node and browsers are hosts that provide different APIs around it.
lessons.lab: Check that the prepared runtime is Node 24 and that process exists.
lessons.verification: major version 24; process.release.name is node. observed value 7 after await.

lessons.title: Values, coercion and precise comparisons
lessons.outcome: JavaScript values have runtime types, and operators can perform implicit conversion.
lessons.lab: Compare 2+3, 2+string 3, and Number(string 3)+2.
lessons.verification: 5, string 23, and 5. valid 12 accepted; invalid cases throw.

lessons.title: Control flow and loop boundaries
lessons.outcome: Control flow decides which expressions execute and how many times.
lessons.lab: Inspect Boolean conversions of 0, empty string, empty array and empty object.
lessons.verification: false, false, true, true. extra undefined element exposes the off-by-one.

lessons.title: Functions, scope and closures
lessons.outcome: Functions define reusable computations, and lexical scope determines which bindings a function can read.
lessons.lab: Use add with 2, 3 and with negative 1, 1.
lessons.verification: 5 and 0. TypeError for 0 and 1.5; step 2 yields 2, 4.

lessons.title: Arrays and immutable transformations
lessons.outcome: Array operations differ in whether they mutate the container, return a new container or reuse referenced objects.
lessons.lab: Double 1, 2, 3, 4 and keep results above 4.
lessons.verification: 6, 8; original array unchanged. edited record changes; original record stays 1.

lessons.title: Objects, properties and prototypes
lessons.outcome: Objects associate property keys with values and can inherit properties through a prototype chain.
lessons.lab: Create a child inheriting kind and owning name.
lessons.verification: kind found by in but not hasOwn; name is own. values 1 then 2; getter executed twice.

lessons.title: Maps, sets and collection identity
lessons.outcome: Map and Set provide collection contracts different from plain object records.
lessons.lab: Create two {id: 1} objects and use them as Map keys.
lessons.verification: size 2 and separate values. b, a, c.

lessons.title: Strings, Unicode and regular expressions
lessons.outcome: JavaScript strings are sequences of UTF-16 code units.
lessons.lab: Inspect A followed by one emoji.
lessons.verification: length 3; spread count 2. item_1 accepted; oversized input rejected.

lessons.title: Errors and explicit validation
lessons.outcome: Errors should distinguish an invalid request from an expected missing result and an operational failure.
lessons.lab: Validate id A, quantity 2, price 125 and calculate integer cents.
lessons.verification: total 250; fresh accepted object. input unchanged.

lessons.title: Modules and dependency boundaries
lessons.outcome: A module is both a namespace and a dependency boundary.
lessons.lab: Import a mutable counter and its increment function, then inspect the count before and after incrementing.
lessons.verification: count changes from 0 to 1 through the imported namespace. TypeError; exported value remains 3.

lessons.title: Iterators and generators
lessons.outcome: An iterable describes how to obtain an iterator.
lessons.lab: Create a generator, inspect its trace, then request one value.
lessons.verification: trace is empty before next; then started, with value 2. empty array for 0; RangeError for -1 and 1.5.

lessons.title: Promises and the event loop
lessons.outcome: A Promise records one eventual settlement: fulfillment with a value or rejection with a reason.
lessons.lab: Record executor, synchronous continuation and then reaction.
lessons.verification: executor, sync, reaction. sync,promise,microtask,timer.

lessons.title: Async functions and cancellation
lessons.outcome: Cancellation is a request communicated to cooperating code.
lessons.lab: Start a timer with a signal, abort it, and inspect the rejection.
lessons.verification: AbortError with the original reason as cause. combined signal is aborted with deadline reason.

lessons.title: Collections, search and algorithmic complexity
lessons.outcome: An algorithm is a rule for transforming an input into a result; complexity describes how its required work grows with input size.
lessons.lab: Find the first insertion position for 4 in 1,4,4,8 and inspect the visited intervals.
lessons.verification: index 1; intervals shrink to the first duplicate. all invariants hold; invalid value throws.

lessons.title: Testing with Node built-ins
lessons.outcome: Tests make a behavioral claim executable.
lessons.lab: Start a real node --test process asserting add(2,3)=5.
lessons.verification: child exit status 0; one passing test. two tests pass without shared mutable state.

lessons.title: Files, paths and streaming text
lessons.outcome: A filesystem path names a resource in a host filesystem.
lessons.lab: Write one line containing an emoji, then compare text length and byte length.
lessons.verification: text round-trips; UTF-8 byte length exceeds code-unit length. no lines.

lessons.title: HTTP, URLs and JSON boundaries
lessons.outcome: HTTP transfers representations between a client and a server using a method, target, headers, status and body.
lessons.lab: GET /sum with a=2 and b=3 and inspect status, content type and JSON.
lessons.verification: status 200; application/json; total 5. status 400 rather than a rounded success value.

lessons.title: A reliable command-line data tool
lessons.outcome: A reliable command-line program has an input contract, an output contract and a failure contract.
lessons.lab: Send two rows worth 250 and 300 cents to the CLI.
lessons.verification: exit 0; stdout is exactly one JSON result with 2 rows and 550 cents; stderr empty. exit 2 with input limit diagnostic; stdout empty.

lessons.title: TypeScript values and compile-time types
lessons.outcome: TypeScript adds a static checker to JavaScript.
lessons.lab: Define a function accepting two numbers and returning their sum; inspect its runtime value.
lessons.verification: sum 5 with runtime typeof number. 12 doubles to 24; string 12 and Infinity reject.

lessons.title: Unions, narrowing and exhaustiveness
lessons.outcome: A union type describes a value that may belong to one of several alternatives.
lessons.lab: Format both successful value 7 and a failure message.
lessons.verification: value:7 and error:offline. runtime fallback throws rather than fabricating success.

lessons.title: Object types and structural contracts
lessons.outcome: TypeScript object types describe the properties an operation requires.
lessons.lab: Pass a wider named object with id and count to a function requiring only id.
lessons.verification: label A; original count remains 2. new array 2,4; input remains 1,2.

lessons.title: Generic functions and constraints
lessons.outcome: Generics express a relationship between types across a reusable operation.
lessons.lab: Pass a number and an object through identity.
lessons.verification: number remains 7; object is the same reference. expected compile error for returning a fabricated length-only object.

lessons.title: Mapped, conditional and utility types
lessons.outcome: Type operators can derive one static description from another, reducing duplicated declarations that drift apart.
lessons.lab: Create a boolean flag type from id and count fields.
lessons.verification: id true and count false; a missing flag is a compile error. valid table remains usable; misspelled literal key is a compiler error.

lessons.title: Runtime validation and unknown input
lessons.outcome: An external payload should enter typed code as unknown.
lessons.lab: Parse an order with two line items and inspect the typed success.
lessons.verification: success with total quantity 5; independent copied item records. every malformed fixture is rejected; an empty items array remains valid.

lessons.title: Typed modules and NodeNext resolution
lessons.outcome: TypeScript source participates in two related dependency graphs: the compiler resolves source and declarations while checking, and Node resolves emitted JavaScript while running.
lessons.lab: Compile a main module importing twice from ./math.mjs and run it.
lessons.verification: both processes succeed; output 8; math.mjs is emitted. value dependency remains; runtime prints ready:A.

lessons.title: Classes, composition and private state
lessons.outcome: Classes combine state with operations that preserve invariants.
lessons.lab: Start with 100 cents, deposit 50 and withdraw 30.
lessons.verification: balance 120; no enumerable balance field. ordinary property 999; private cents remain 2.

lessons.title: Typed async workflows and errors
lessons.outcome: Promise<T> describes a fulfilled value.
lessons.lab: Look up a known id and an absent id.
lessons.verification: known value 7; absent error not_found. expected diagnostics for value before await or before narrowing.

lessons.title: Data structures and dynamic programming
lessons.outcome: Types clarify an algorithm's interface, but correctness depends on its invariant.
lessons.lab: Search a graph with two equal-length routes from A to D.
lessons.verification: A,B,D under the stated neighbor order. RangeError for all invalid configurations; empty denominations cannot make 1.

lessons.title: The DOM, events and accessible interaction
lessons.outcome: The Document Object Model is a live tree of nodes exposed by the browser.
lessons.lab: Open the complete snippet, activate Add twice by pointer and once by keyboard, then inspect the count.
lessons.verification: count 3; button remains keyboard reachable. null is detected before accessing a property.

lessons.title: Forms, browser storage and application state
lessons.outcome: A form is a structured input interface, not merely a collection of text boxes.
lessons.lab: Save the snippet as HTML and submit name Ada and quantity 2, then try an invalid quantity.
lessons.verification: valid output Ada: 2; invalid input produces no accepted state. owned key absent; unrelated key unchanged.

lessons.title: Safe browser rendering and security boundaries
lessons.outcome: Rendering untrusted text is a data-versus-code boundary.
lessons.lab: Save the snippet and inspect the resulting DOM and visible title.
lessons.verification: the angle-bracket text is visible; no img element is created. no claim that CSP authenticates callers, CORS authorizes actions, or meta implements frame-ancestors.

lessons.title: Streams and backpressure
lessons.outcome: A stream transports chunks incrementally between a producer and a consumer.
lessons.lab: Uppercase two byte chunks and collect the transformed output.
lessons.verification: ABCD after successful pipeline completion. pipeline rejects with AbortError; generator finally runs.

lessons.title: Worker threads and CPU-bound work
lessons.outcome: An async function does not automatically move CPU work off the main JavaScript thread.
lessons.lab: Sum integers 1 through 10000 in a worker and inspect its thread id.
lessons.verification: sum 50005000; worker thread id positive. DataCloneError before useful worker execution.

lessons.title: Memory, performance and profiling
lessons.outcome: Performance measurement begins with a correctness contract and a question.
lessons.lab: Sum a fixed numeric range and record elapsed duration.
lessons.verification: correct sum 50005000; finite nonnegative elapsed time. monitor disabled afterward; sample count reported honestly.

lessons.title: Dates, internationalization and time zones
lessons.outcome: A date-time problem can involve an instant, a calendar date, a local clock reading or a duration.
lessons.lab: Parse UTC midnight and the equivalent previous-day offset representation.
lessons.verification: equal timestamps and UTC ISO output. NaN timestamp; toISOString and invalid timezone construction throw RangeError.

lessons.title: Package design and reproducible toolchains
lessons.outcome: A package is a public interface plus the files and metadata needed to implement it.
lessons.lab: Create a package with exports pointing at index.mjs and import its version value.
lessons.verification: actual child prints 1. child exits successfully for twice(0)=0 and twice(-2)=-4.

lessons.title: Network retries, idempotency and bounded concurrency
lessons.outcome: A retry is a new attempt after an uncertain or failed operation.
lessons.lab: Fail twice transiently, then succeed, using random value 0.5 and a recording wait.
lessons.verification: three attempts; delays 50 and 100; result ready. original reason rejects; attempts remain 0.

lessons.title: Typed API design and contract testing
lessons.outcome: A typed API contract connects request validation, domain behavior, transport status and response decoding.
lessons.lab: Send 2 and 3 through the handler, JSON round-trip its reply, then decode it.
lessons.verification: status 200 and decoded total 5. bad_request response does not echo the supplied value.

lessons.title: Functional core and state machines
lessons.outcome: A state machine makes allowed transitions explicit.
lessons.lab: Start a queued job and complete it with value 7.
lessons.verification: succeeded with attempt 1 and value 7. input unchanged; new object returned; NaN rejects.

lessons.title: A tested local JavaScript service
lessons.outcome: A local service combines transport handling with domain state and resource ownership.
lessons.lab: POST item A with value 2, then GET the list.
lessons.verification: 201 created; subsequent 200 list contains exactly A. matching id and status; server no longer listening.

lessons.title: A typed analytics pipeline
lessons.outcome: An analytics pipeline combines framing, parsing, validation and aggregation.
lessons.lab: Decode rows for groups A and B from three-byte chunks and aggregate their values.
lessons.verification: A count 2 sum 5; B count 1 sum 4; zero rejected. zero accepted with one rejected versus zero accepted with zero rejected.

lessons.title: Release, observability and maintenance
lessons.outcome: A release is a specific artifact with a reproducible behavior contract, not merely a folder that once worked during development.
lessons.lab: Create the authored bundle, verify hashes and run its self-test in a child.
lessons.verification: three checks passed; actual Node version reported. matching policy passes; mismatched policy throws.
